first.rationale: Two of three current signals (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) point directly at the onboarding funnel, and memory_31/memory_86 both report durable, replicated gains from simplifying/shortening onboarding across self-serve SMB accounts—this is the most directly diagnostic and lowest-risk use of the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but it optimizes for immediate SMB acquisition and could pull in more price-sensitive, lower-LTV accounts, working against the 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective; I want the archived record on memory_73 checked before ever running it, since it's the more consequential and risk-laden lever. I'm also verifying memory_31 because it's the oldest/most heavily relied-upon memory driving this decision and the current 4-6% declines suggest something may have shifted since day 12 that a full re-read of the source could reveal. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist are not responsive to the immediate SMB/activation problem and are deprioritized this cycle. Given competing pressures and incomplete verification, I'm sizing this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, preserving the option to pivot toward pricing defense next cycle if onboarding fixes don't address the competitive SMB erosion.
